gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-14 BLUETTI's US store sells the AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W) for $499, the same price as its 1,024 Wh Elite 100 V2 and $30.99 under the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 on Amazon ($529.99), while ChatGPT showed the AC180 at $998 in two chats; EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Classic is the cheapest 1,800 W option at $459.
standout_why: I read the cited rival pages. keeplights.com (microwave guide, updated 2026-10-23) gives runtimes for the AC180, Explorer 1000 v2, C1000 Gen 2 and DELTA 3 but no prices. powerstationtips.com has stale 'from' prices (AC180 'from ~$699', DELTA 2 'from ~$999'). outletpowered.com lists no prices. backuppowerfinder.com lists no prices. backup-power.org (cited) already says the AC180 and Elite 100 V2 cost 'just under $500' on BLUETTI's store, but gives no check date and never mentions microwaves. Because backup-power.org has part of the price finding, this scores 1. No rival puts dated store prices next to inverter headroom and minutes per charge for each microwave candidate, and ChatGPT's own cards were wrong ($998 for the AC180).
decides: The finding confirms the Anker C1000 Gen 2 as the pick for microwaves drawing 1,600 to 2,000 W, since it is the only 2,000 W unit here with a sourced price ($529.99 on Amazon). It also adds a cheaper pick for microwaves drawing up to about 1,600 W: the BLUETTI AC180 at $499. For the same money as the Elite 100 V2 it has 128 Wh more, which works out to about 39 minutes instead of 35 at a 1,500 W draw (85% usable). The DELTA 3 Classic at $459 is the lowest price for 1,800 W. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 drops out of the full-size microwave pick because of its 1,500 W limit.
